description: Hold the headpond within license limits; open and close the 2 spillway gates in high flows; automatic level control by the gate PLC; gate moves from the HMI or the local panels
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Public safety first: an unplanned gate movement changes flows at the tailrace and canoe launch, and loss of gate control in a flood risks overtopping. With 7 staff the company can keep a person at the hoist house panels around the clock for about 8 hours before fatigue and coverage become unsafe. Gate PLC logic changes rarely, so a copy no older than the last approved change (daily target) is enough
manual_workaround: Switch gates to local control at the hoist house panels; an operator-mechanic stays at the panels; move gates only on the Plant Superintendent's instruction; call in off-duty staff; call the integrator
dependent_third_parties: Controls integrator; standby generator fuel supplier

business_process: Dam safety monitoring, public warning, and EAP notification
description: Collect headwater, tailwater, piezometer, and seepage readings; compare with trigger points; sound the tailrace horn and strobes before releases; make EAP and 18 CFR 12.10 notifications
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Unusual instrument readings are reportable conditions (18 CFR 12.3(b)(4)(viii)); the data logger keeps 60 days of readings, so little data is lost, but trend review needs near-current data. Manual readings must start within 12 hours
manual_workaround: Manual readings of piezometers and weirs every 12 hours with a portable readout; staff gauge for headwater and tailwater; manual switch for the tailrace horn; EAP call-down by phone
dependent_third_parties: Consulting dam safety engineer; county emergency management; cellular carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Plant Superintendent; Operator-Mechanics; hoist house; instrument locations

description: Start, load, and stop the 2 units; governor and excitation control; protective relays; coordinate output with the cooperative
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Generation is almost all of the revenue: about $2,750 a day at average output. Units can run in local control while staff are on site. Past 3 days the loss passes $8,000 and the overnight shutdowns start to wear on equipment
manual_workaround: Run units from the local unit panels while staffed; shut units down overnight and pass water through the gates; ask the integrator for governor settings if a controller is replaced
dependent_third_parties: Controls integrator; governor and exciter manufacturer support; cooperative
dependent_people_or_facilities: Plant Superintendent; Controls and Electrical Technician; powerhouse

business_process: After-hours monitoring, alarm callout, and remote response
description: Overnight alarm callout to the on-call operator-mechanic; remote view and, today, remote operation of the HMI
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The plant is unattended from 17:30 to 07:00. Without callouts a high-water or unit trip alarm could go unanswered for one night. Readings in the monitoring service are kept every minute
manual_workaround: Keep an operator-mechanic in the control room overnight; shut units down overnight if nobody can stay; the gate PLC continues automatic level control
dependent_third_parties: Remote monitoring service vendor; cellular carrier; remote desktop tool vendor

business_process: Physical security and recreation area safety
description: Fence, gates, and locks; camera viewing; patrols of the canoe launch, portage, and bank-fishing area; warning signs and the boat barrier
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cameras and locks deter tampering with the hoist house and powerhouse; recreation users must be kept away from the tailrace during releases
manual_workaround: Extra walk-downs by the operator-mechanic on shift; ask the sheriff for more patrols; close the canoe launch temporarily (FERC notice if for security, Rev. 3A 3.3.4)

description: 18 CFR 12.10 reports, EAP and ODSP updates, license filings, permanent project records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Initial 12.10 reports can be made by telephone; written reports are due when the Regional Engineer directs. Original project records are on paper in the office
manual_workaround: Telephone the Regional Engineer; use paper originals and printed EAP; send written reports once email returns
dependent_third_parties: MSP; productivity suite vendor; consulting dam safety engineer
dependent_people_or_facilities: Office and Compliance Administrator; Plant Superintendent; office

description: Planned outage notices to the cooperative; monthly invoice from the cooperative's meter reads; renewable energy credit records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The cooperative reads its own meter, so energy is never lost from the record; invoices can wait a week. Outage notices can be made by phone
manual_workaround: Phone the cooperative's dispatcher; prepare the invoice from the cooperative's meter statement
dependent_people_or_facilities: Owner and General Manager; Office and Compliance Administrator

business_process: Office administration, email, accounting, and payroll
description: Email, files, accounts payable, payroll every two weeks through the payroll service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs every two weeks and the payroll service can repeat the prior run; a cash reserve covers about 45 days of expenses
manual_workaround: Use phones and personal email only for non-sensitive coordination; ask the payroll service to repeat the prior payroll; pay urgent bills by bank portal
dependent_third_parties: MSP; productivity suite vendor; payroll service; accounting software vendor
